question: Who can appoint the judges of the High Court?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Indian Constitution**, the **President** of India has the authority to appoint judges of the High Court.
 
• The appointment is made after consultation with the **Chief Justice of India** and the **Governor** of the respective state.
 
• This is outlined in **Article 217** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The **President** ensures that the appointed judges possess the necessary qualifications and experience.
 
• The appointed judge must have served as a judge in a court of law for at least **ten years** or have been an advocate in a High Court for a similar period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Attorney General**__

 __
 
• The **Attorney General** is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India.
 
• They are appointed by the **President** and must be a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• The Attorney General does not have the authority to appoint judges.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**__
 __
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the head of the government in India.
 
• While the Prime Minister plays a significant role in the administration, they do not have the power to appoint judges.
 
• The Prime Minister's recommendations might influence the appointment process, but the formal authority lies with the President.
 
 
 
• **Governor**__
 
 
• The **Governor** is the head of a state in India.
 
• They are consulted during the appointment of High Court judges but do not have the final authority to make appointments.
 
• The Governor's role is advisory in the context of judicial appointments.
